neighbours.label: the conjunction ' but' joining two clauses (contrast)
fire: He decided against the move for many reasons, but mainly because of cost.
Each element alone can cause damage, but here several act together.
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving.
The plan looked simple on paper, but it failed in practice.
We searched the whole house, but the keys were never found.
The film was long, but nobody in the audience left early.
Prices rose sharply in spring, but sales stayed strong.
The team played well in the first half, but faded later.
quiet: He decided against the move for many reasons, mainly because of cost.
Each element alone can cause damage, and here several act together.
She wanted to stay longer, so she missed the last train.
The plan looked simple on paper, and it worked in practice.
We searched the whole house, and the keys were found upstairs.
The film was long, so many in the audience left early.
Prices rose sharply in spring, and sales fell as well.
The team played well in the first half, then scored again.
